relations.note: The First Father brings forth Tupã and assigns his dwelling and generative task.
They send names or word-souls and participate in maintaining the cosmos.
She is Tupã Ru Ete’s female divine counterpart and generative partner.
Karai governs fire while Tupã governs waters and storms; no rivalry occurs.
Jakaira governs life-giving mist or smoke while Tupã governs waters and storms.
Arasy is Tupã’s celestial wife.
Tupã and Arasy jointly form and animate the first human couple.
Tupã forms and animates Rupavẽ as the first man.
Tupã blesses and instructs the newly created first man.
Tupã and Arasy form and animate Sypavẽ as the first woman.
Tupã creates or leaves Angatupyry, the principle of goodness, among humanity.
Tupã creates or permits Tau, the principle of evil, as Angatupyry’s opposite.
Tupã is indirectly involved through the moral order and punishment surrounding her seizure.
Tupã stands above the world where Tau and Kerana’s monstrous child is born.
relations.source: Colmán, Ñande Ypy Kuéra; derivative folklore

relations.note: Christian Guaraní calls Jesus Tupã Ra’y, meaning Son of Tupã or God.
Christian Guaraní names Mary Tupãsy, meaning Mother of Tupã or God.
Missionary discourse opposes Tupã as God to Añá as the Devil.
